stimulus.text: Frontispiece to Phillis Wheatley’s Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral (1773), attributed to Scipio Moorhead. The oval portrait shows Wheatley at a desk, holding a quill over a sheet of paper, with an inkwell and a book beside her. The words around the oval read: “PHILLIS WHEATLEY, NEGRO SERVANT to Mr. JOHN WHEATLEY, of BOSTON.”

stem: The words around the oval in the frontispiece show that Wheatley’s book was presented to readers as the work of...

options.text: a free white woman of Boston.
options.misconception: The words call her a Negro servant, not a free white woman.

options.text: an enslaved Black woman writing while in bondage.

options.misconception: The words name her as a servant of John Wheatley of Boston, not a British visitor.

options.text: an anonymous author whose name was kept secret.
options.misconception: Her name appears in large letters around the oval.

rationales.B: The border reads “PHILLIS WHEATLEY, NEGRO SERVANT to Mr. JOHN WHEATLEY, of BOSTON.”
rationales.A: The words say Negro servant, which is the opposite of a free white woman.
rationales.C: The words tie her to John Wheatley of Boston, not to Britain.
rationales.D: Her name is printed around the oval for every reader to see.
rationales.general:
1. The words around the oval name Phillis Wheatley and call her a Negro servant to John Wheatley of Boston.
2. The portrait shows her at a desk with a quill, inkwell, and book.
3. Background: Wheatley was still enslaved when her book appeared in 1773.
4. So the book reached readers as the work of an enslaved Black woman writer.
Remember: a book’s frontispiece tells you how its author was presented to readers.
